Every other key belongs to the IOLS record. The complete IOLS table lists all nine controls, defaults and constructor versus execution domains. Print pm.solver_defaults("iols").to_dict() to inspect your installation.

The key iols_backend requests an implementation: "cpp" for the compiled extension or "numpy". Omit it for automatic selection. An explicit "cpp" request is refused when the compiled extension is unavailable. result.provenance.trace records requested_backend, actual_backend and fallback_used; read them rather than assuming which implementation ran.

Passing the typed default record preserves omitted implementation selection. Its backend_explicit property tells you whether a backend was requested. To construct a typed record from chosen options, use type(pm.solver_defaults("iols")).from_dict({"stopcrit": 5000}). Passing its complete .to_dict() mapping instead makes "cpp" explicit, because that mapping contains iols_backend. On a NumPy-only installation, use the typed record or explicitly request "numpy". The installation guide explains this distinction.

IOLS refuses settings outside its no-FE scope, listed in numerical methods. It does not select tau and does not change the Newton default.

Experimental absorption options

With fixed effects, the iteration also solves weighted within-group problems. Fixed-effect fits use the additional controls below for that work. These are not ordinary no-FE solver keywords.

Option Default Role
absorbed "profiled" Choose "index" to request the index organization explicitly.
absorb_tol_start 1e-4 Positive finite starting absorption tolerance.
absorb_tol_final 2e-11 Positive finite final absorption tolerance.
absorb_max_sweeps 20000 Positive integer sweep limit.
absorb_acceleration True Boolean acceleration choice.
profile_tol 2e-11 Positive finite profiling tolerance.
profile_max_sweeps 20000 Positive integer profiling sweep limit.

Ordinary joint and cancelled fits use the package’s default sample and numerical controls. To customize them, use SampleRequest for a joint fit or CancelledFitControls for a cancelled fit. The advanced FE options describes these records. FE fits use Newton; solver="iols" is refused with fixed effects.

Larger budgets are not a remedy for nonidentification, separation or a wrong model. A numerical threshold does not establish coefficient parity, coverage or a universal error bound. Preserve the actual failure and review its cause.

Use Troubleshooting to distinguish an unavailable request, a sample problem and an unsuccessful numerical solve.

Advanced fixed-effect options

Routine fits use the formula and defaults from the fixed effects chapter. The optional module-level control records in this reference are experimental.

Use the default settings for an ordinary fixed-effect call. Supply a solver_options record to choose the organization or control sample construction for the cases below.

Formula and call shapes

Use pm.fit and specify the supported equation. Write FE blocks after |, for example "y ~ 0 + x | firm + year". The slope intercept is omitted here because the group indicators already span a constant.

The calls below use a frame with columns y, x, firm, year and unit. The first estimates both blocks jointly. The second cancels the firm block, estimates year effects and uses the cancelled groups for its default covariance.

import powermean as pm

joint = pm.fit(
    "y ~ 0 + x | firm + year", data,
    omega=1, tau=1, cluster="unit",
)
cancelled = pm.fit(
    "y ~ 0 + x | firm + year", data,
    omega=1, tau=1, cancel="firm",
)

At omega=1, tau=1, joint and cancelled PPML have the same uncorrected slopes on the same retained sample. Each positive-total firm’s fitted values sum to its observed total. This equation determines its intercept at each Newton step. When the admitted fixed effects permit that calculation, the default zero-start cancelled fit uses the joint solver to perform it. The solver trace records the steps it actually took. The cancelled fit checks its own score and reports the requested covariance and bias correction.

To select an organization explicitly, pass solver_options={"absorbed": "index"} or solver_options={"absorbed": "profiled"} to pm.fit. Omitting it uses "profiled". Within that mapping, a joint call can supply an already constructed SampleRequest under "sample_request". A cancelled call can supply a CancelledFitControls record under "controls". The resolver describes these experimental module-level records.

Any one block can be cancelled by name. Use cancel=True to select the unique block with the most levels. A cancelled pm.fit call that omits both tau and variance uses tau=2, so state the working variance explicitly when comparing calls.

Joint sample controls

A joint fit first constructs the sample appropriate to its mean order and working variance. SampleRequest requires all eight fields:

Field Requirement
omega Current mean order; must match the fit.
positive_only Current prepared outcome domain; must match the fit.
variance Matching PowerVariance or NB2Variance at nonzero order; None at order zero.
keep_singletons Explicit Boolean governing that sample step.
support Actual SupportControls for power 1 <= tau < 2 or NB2; otherwise None.
recession Actual LPControls for power tau=2; otherwise None.
collinearity Actual diagnostic controls for the FE sample.
mode "drop" or "error" for collinearity.

For power tau < 1 or tau > 2 at a nonzero order, both existence controls are None: sample construction runs rank checks only, without an existence analysis.

These records govern ordered sample construction. They are not saved success flags for another sample, order or variance. Inspect the actual sample accounting. Keeping singletons does not disable subsequent identification or existence checks.

Cancellation controls

A cancelled fit has its own geometry and numerical work controls. To override the defaults, supply a CancelledFitControls record with ten fields:

Field Role
gram_rtol Geometry rank threshold.
gap_min Required geometry spectral gap.
geometry_bytes Geometry allocation budget.
admission_bytes Admission allocation budget.
identity_atol Numerical identity comparison threshold.
attempt AttemptBounds for the numerical attempt.
certificate AttemptBounds for its assessment.
inference AttemptBounds for inference work.
diagnostic Collinearity/absorption diagnostic controls.
collinear Explicit collinearity policy.

AttemptBounds(max_bytes=..., max_work=...) requires positive Python integers. Its byte limit reserves specified numerical buffers; it is not a hard limit on process memory. Provider workspace, Python objects and other storage can lie outside that reservation. See the constructor.

Choose custom controls for the scale and purpose of your analysis. A large budget does not resolve a failure of identification.

Other numerical records

After those input requirements, the requested variance determines the computational procedure. Cancellation at omega=0 is refused; log OLS uses its separate additive formulation. Execution for a supported cancelled model is recorded in result.provenance.options["route"]: "convex_tau2" for power variance tau=2, "absorbed_tau1" for tau=1 or NB2 with zero kappa, and "root_newton" otherwise. These are computational labels, not different estimands to choose after a failure. The absorbed_options affect the absorbed tau-one calculation; other branches use their own recorded controls.

solver_options can also contain the ordinary solver options record, absorbed_options and root_options, a RootOptions record or its mapping. Equivalent flat and nested explicit settings must agree. A cancelled call may use root_options. A joint call reads it only for a power tau outside [1, 2] at a nonzero order and refuses it otherwise; flat root keys are unknown to FE calls. A joint call refuses cancellation controls, and a cancelled call refuses sample_request. A joint call may add max_dense_bytes, a positive integer ceiling for the WZ numeric buffers of the fit and of its later covariance requests; a cancelled call refuses it. FE fits use Newton; solver="iols" is refused.

On that selected-root route, a joint fit starts from a certified tau=1 fit (below 1) or tau=2 fit (above 2) of the same sample, at the requested mean order and computed by the requested organization, unless start is supplied. At omega=1 these are PPML and GPML. It then runs sparse root Newton on the full joint equation. Its settings sit beside "absorbed" and "sample_request", for example "root_options": {"merit_metric": "gram"}. It issues a CoverageWarning where the root is not characterized. result.provenance.options records operation and the resolved root_options, and result.provenance.trace records the initializer and the stage path.

The root record, shared by cancellation and the selected-root routes, has root_armijo=1e-4, root_max_backtracks=60, root_max_iter=200, merit_metric="gamma", continuation="fallback" and continuation_step=0.5. These specify a root procedure, not permission to change the estimator after failure. This table does not claim broad scientific validation of every continuation path.

Coefficient corrections

bias_correction requests a coefficient correction for an FE fit; ordinary no-FE calls accept only False. A correction is evaluated once at the certified uncorrected root, without refitting. A domain that is not established is refused rather than replaced by a zero correction.

Request Fit Requirements
False (default) Any No correction work runs.
True or "short_group" Cancelled Short-group correction of Benatia et al. (2026), with cancelled groups as the sampling units.
"cell" Cancelled Cell correction of Benatia et al. (2026). Without vcov, the sampling units are the cancelled groups; a declared one-way classification that consists of complete cancelled groups is the sampling unit.
"wz" Joint or cancelled The correction of Weidner and Zylkin (2021) for PPML, omega=1 and tau=1, with observed bread and no weights.

Powermean supplies the coefficient corrections of Benatia et al. (2026) for cancelled fits. A vcov request that declares no sampling of the correction (robust, named HC, several dimensions, a classification that crosses the cancelled groups, or one coarser than them beside True or "short_group") is answered at the fit as with_vcov answers it after the fit: the correction at the cancelled groups and the requested covariance at the uncorrected root, with the same estimates, covariance and diagnostic notes. The corrections use the cancelled fit’s working variance and their own numerical checks.

The analytical coefficient and covariance adjustments follow Weidner and Zylkin (2021), §§3.4.2–3.4.3. Published paper

For three-way PPML, the WZ correction needs an identifiable directed pair block. Name the pair cluster explicitly if the formula leaves its role ambiguous. The correction requires the same set of at least three countries on the origin and destination sides and at least two dates. Each retained directed pair must appear once at every observed date. Whole pairs may be absent, and diagonal pairs may be present or absent.

A joint fit must keep its original unconditioned sample: no positive-only restriction, conditioning or recorded sample-construction change. A cancelled fit must be unconditioned, cancel that pair block and keep every slope identified. Without a vcov request, the covariance becomes the pair cluster with adjustment="wz". An explicit request must cluster on the pair; adding "adjustment": "none" keeps the ordinary pair covariance.

coef(), the estimate column of tidy(), effects, contrasts and tests use the corrected coefficients. tidy() adds uncorrected and bias, and summary() prints the decomposition. The certificate refers to the uncorrected root; se(), vcov() and intervals use the first-order covariance evaluated there. provenance.options["bias_correction"] records the correction. If the root is not certified, the coefficients and the correction are withheld.

After a WZ correction, fixef() and predict() are outputs of the original uncorrected root; corrected slopes are not combined with original effects. Their attrs record evaluation_point="original uncorrected estimating root" and nuisance_correction="not_supplied". After a short-group or cell correction, cancelled predictions and effects use the corrected reporting point.

The WZ covariance adjustment is a separate request: vcov={"cluster": pair, "adjustment": "wz"}, where pair names the pair block, at fit time or through vcov(spec) and with_vcov(spec). At fit time it requires builtin PPML, observed bread and a named ssc preset; with cancellation, cancel must name that pair block. The returned vcov().attrs record adjustment="wz", coefficient_correction=False and covariance_point="uncorrected root".

Current inference and result limits

Joint and cancelled calls accept robust, named HC ("HC0" to "HC5" and "HC4m") and one-way or multiway cluster requests, subject to the method’s requirements. Cancelled calls use observed bread. A named HC request on a cancelled call is evaluated once at the accepted point, with or without bias_correction.

For example, a cancelled fit can use vcov={"cluster": "country + family", "multiway": "cgm", "psd": "none"} with ssc="none" for the unadjusted signed two-way covariance. To request the same covariance after a fit, retain the cluster labels and the influence contributions. influence(unit="row") returns the original-row contributions in estimation-sample order. The default influence() returns one contribution per cancelled group.

Fixed-effect calls refuse supplied observation weights, even if all values equal one. HAC and Conley computation are deferred.

Joint fixef() returns estimated normalized effects. Cancelled fixef() returns the retained blocks and, under the cancelled block’s name, effects recovered in sample at the stored point; results describes their status labels and how they are used in prediction. A failed fit retains its actual status and diagnostics.

Preparation remains order neutral. Each fit still needs controls consistent with its requested order, family and formulation. See cancellation, results and availability.

If a request is refused, Troubleshooting explains what to inspect before changing it.

IOLS solver options (IolsOptions)

powermean.solver_defaults("iols") returns a fresh powermean.solve.iols.options.IolsOptions record with the default settings for solver="iols".

Option Type Default Constructor domain Execution / resolver rule Description
eps float 1e-12 positive finite real numbers positive finite real numbers Stops iteration when the largest coefficient change is below the threshold; the final residual check determines whether the solution has converged.
anderson_m int 5 nonnegative integers nonnegative integers Initial depth of the Anderson mixing; a nonnegative integer, zero included, stored as given and not a statement about the source’s later adaptation of the depth.
max_phase1_iterations int 100000 positive integers integers >= 2 at execution (max_phase1_iterations=1 is accepted by IolsOptions construction but refused by options_to_kernel_control with specification.invalid_value; no silent clamping) Budget of pilot updates; a positive integer, 1 included.
stopcrit int 1000000 positive integers integers >= 2 at execution (stopcrit=1 is accepted by IolsOptions construction but refused by options_to_kernel_control with specification.invalid_value; no silent clamping) Budget of updates per step size; a positive integer, 1 included.
max_phase2_evaluations int 5000000 positive integers integers >= 1 (max_phase2_evaluations=1 is accepted at both construction and execution mapping) Budget of evaluations of the exact map; a positive integer, 1 included.
delta_grid tuple[float, ...] [0.006737946999085467, 0.0820849986238988, 1.0, 12.182493960703473, 148.4131591025766] nonempty lists, tuples or one-dimensional arrays of positive finite real numbers nonempty 1D sequence of positive finite reals (stored as tuple[float, ...], serialized as list[float], preserving order and duplicate entries) The shifts of the pilot, in their order and with their repetitions; a nonempty list, tuple or one-dimensional array of positive finite reals, stored as a tuple of floats; neither sorted, deduplicated nor rebuilt from endpoints.
rho_log_min float -7.0 finite real numbers unbounded finite real numbers (lower=null, upper=null in JSON metadata; independent of the opposite bound) Logarithmic lower bound of the step grid; a finite real, independent of rho_log_max and not exponentiated here.
rho_log_max float 14.0 finite real numbers unbounded finite real numbers (lower=null, upper=null in JSON metadata; independent of the opposite bound) Logarithmic upper bound of the step grid; a finite real, independent of rho_log_min and not exponentiated here.
iols_backend literal["cpp", "numpy"] "cpp" ‘cpp’, ‘numpy’ 'cpp', 'numpy' (omitted prefers 'cpp' and falls back to 'numpy' only when powermean._native.iols._kernel_cpp is absent on disk; explicit 'cpp' is strict; internal 'auto' is refused) The implementation: the compiled full loop or its NumPy twin, an explicit and recorded choice.

Execution and implementation rules

  • Constructor budgets vs. execution mapping (options_to_kernel_control). IolsOptions validates max_phase1_iterations, stopcrit, and max_phase2_evaluations as positive integers (>= 1) at construction. When mapping to IOLSKernelControl for execution, max_phase1_iterations < 2 and stopcrit < 2 are refused with SpecificationError("specification.invalid_value") rather than clamped; max_phase2_evaluations = 1 remains valid at execution.
  • Backend omission vs. explicit selection (backend_explicit). Public iols_backend values are 'cpp' and 'numpy' only; internal 'auto' is not a valid public literal and is refused. When iols_backend is omitted (IolsOptions() or IolsOptions.from_dict({})), iols_backend equals 'cpp', backend_explicit is False, and effective_backend_request is 'auto', preferring 'cpp' and falling back to 'numpy' only when powermean._native.iols._kernel_cpp is absent on disk. When iols_backend='cpp' is supplied explicitly, backend_explicit is True and 'cpp' selection is strict without fallback. Because IolsOptions.to_dict() returns a complete mapping that includes 'iols_backend', passing opts.to_dict() back to IolsOptions.from_dict(...) or solver_options supplies 'cpp' explicitly (backend_explicit=True).
  • Ordered pilot grid (delta_grid). delta_grid accepts any nonempty list, tuple, or 1D array of positive finite real numbers and stores a tuple[float, ...] preserving the caller’s exact order and duplicate entries without sorting, deduplicating, or reconstructing from endpoints.
  • Unbounded finite-real logarithmic step bounds (rho_log_min, rho_log_max). Both bounds accept any finite real number (lower=null, upper=null in exported JSON domain metadata; non-finite values and Booleans are refused) and are not ordered against each other.
  • Certificate keys alongside IOLS options. When solver='iols' and solver_options is passed as a mapping, the certificate keys (coef_tol, rcond_min, tol, tol_secondary) are resolved through SolverOptions while all IOLS-specific keys are resolved through IolsOptions.

When slope scaling stops the solve

Before the first iteration, IOLS checks the centered standard deviation of each slope in its input units. A positive SD below the larger of 1e-12 × largest slope SD and 1e-300 stops the solve with status solver_error. The default raises ConvergenceError. With on_failure="return", result.provenance.failure records the first affected slope name and its index (zero-based, excluding the intercept), its SD, the maximum SD, the floor and zero iterations and evaluations. The result has no fitted point or certificate, and inference is withheld. Changing a predictor’s units can cross this floor while preserving the rank of the design.

Install and troubleshoot no-FE IOLS

Powermean provides a compiled implementation of the complete no-fixed-effects IOLS iteration loop and a corresponding NumPy implementation. Newton remains the default solver; installing an IOLS extension does not change that default.

Choose the artifact before installing

Choose a wheel for your Python version, operating system and architecture. Use a compiled wheel if you want to require the C++ IOLS backend. The wheel name identifies the Python and platform tags; check the artifact description to distinguish a compiled build from a NumPy-only build.

Start in a separate, compatible Python environment with the dependencies declared by the package already available. A local, offline wheel-installation recipe is:

python -m pip install --no-index --no-deps --no-compile \
    ./artifacts/powermean-*.whl

Put only the selected wheel in artifacts. This offline command uses the dependencies already in your environment. For normal dependency resolution, follow the installation guide.

Check the installed IOLS implementation

Run the example script using the Python environment where you installed Powermean:

python docs/examples/iols_first_fit.py --backend auto

The script creates a fixed-seed, 240-row simulated sample, requests no-FE PPML with IOLS and robust covariance, and prints the coefficient table and actual implementation. On a compiled build, the solver information includes:

Solver: iols
requested_backend: auto
actual_backend: cpp
fallback_used: False

The script’s --backend auto means that it omits iols_backend from the package request. It does not pass iols_backend="auto", which is not a public option value. With automatic selection, the example reports numpy on a NumPy-only build. Use the reported backend to confirm which one ran.

Select the implementation deliberately

For an IOLS fit, solver="iols" selects IOLS. Within solver_options, the only public iols_backend values are "cpp" and "numpy":

  • Omit the backend to prefer C++. Automatic NumPy selection is allowed only when the exact powermean._native.iols._kernel_cpp module is genuinely absent.
  • Supply iols_backend="cpp" to require C++. Its absence or failure is an error, not permission to switch implementations.
  • Supply iols_backend="numpy" to select NumPy intentionally.

pm.solver_defaults("iols") returns a typed options record. Its default backend value is "cpp", but the record separately retains that the caller omitted the backend. Passing that typed record preserves omission. Passing its complete .to_dict() mapping supplies the backend explicitly and therefore requires C++. This distinction matters on a NumPy-only installation.

Inspect the returned result’s provenance rather than inferring which implementation ran from the package name or an iteration count. A broken native extension, exhausted budget or failed numerical assessment does not cause a retry with NumPy or Newton.

Source-build requirements

A source build is distinct from installing a compatible wheel. Its declared build requirements are installed by pip when it builds in isolation. The CMake configuration uses installed native libraries and headers.

The compiled target uses C++17, Python development-module support, pybind11 and Eigen headers supplied by cmeel-eigen or a local installation. On Linux and Windows it uses its Eigen JacobiSVD least-squares branch and links no LAPACK library unless an OpenBLAS library is explicitly supplied through POWERMEAN_IOLS_OPENBLAS64_LIBRARY. On macOS the build links the build NumPy’s scipy-openblas64 library when it finds one in NumPy’s numpy.libs folder, and otherwise requires an existing LAPACK implementation. Set EIGEN3_INCLUDE_DIR if CMake cannot find the existing Eigen headers.

POWERMEAN_BUILD_IOLS is the CMake switch for including the IOLS extension and is ON by default. Selecting OFF omits that target; it does not establish a compiler-free build or a platform-independent wheel. The current root CMake project still declares the C++ language.

Troubleshooting without changing the requested model

Observation Meaning and appropriate next step
The example reports NumPy when selection was omitted On a NumPy-only artifact this is expected. Check the supplied artifact manifest and the recorded actual backend.
Explicit C++ fails because its exact module is absent The installed artifact cannot satisfy that explicit request. Use a compatible compiled artifact, or explicitly request NumPy if that is what you intend.
Import reports a missing transitive dependency, incompatible ABI or missing symbol This is not extension absence. Correct the installation or library compatibility; automatic fallback is not applied.
The module lacks a required entry point Install the wheel for your Python version and platform.
iols_backend="auto" is refused Omit the option for automatic availability-based selection. "auto" is an internal request label, not a public literal.
A typed default works but its .to_dict() mapping fails without C++ The complete mapping made C++ explicit. Pass the typed record to preserve omission, or explicitly request NumPy.
A budget of one constructs successfully but is refused when fitting Construction and execution have distinct domains: max_phase1_iterations and stopcrit require at least two for execution; max_phase2_evaluations=1 remains valid. Values are not silently clamped.
IOLS refuses FE, weights, offsets, exposure, instruments or a supplied start This no-FE solver does not support those requests. This is a capability refusal, not a broken installation or a reason for hidden solver substitution.
A fitted solution fails its convergence or inference checks An installed extension is not a guarantee of a verified fit. Keep the failure visible; changing implementation or weakening a check is not an automatic recovery step.

The supported IOLS domain uses positive omega, power working variance with tau in [1, 2], a unit intercept, at least one slope and more observations than design columns. NB2, log OLS, cancellation and bias correction are not supported by this route. The package’s separate FE/cancellation work does not expand this solver’s domain.

Use the IOLS option reference for all nine controls and their domains. Report the small public call, the relevant exception and the implementation provenance when asking for help; do not share credentials, private observations or a complete environment dump.

Diagnose errors and unsuccessful fits

Start with the exception class, the full diagnostic and the formula. A single change to the outcome transformation or retained rows can change the quantity being estimated.

Symptom Inspect
SpecificationError Unknown or conflicting options, formula syntax and method requirements.
SampleError Negative outcomes, zeros at a nonpositive mean order, negative weights, or an empty estimation sample.
ValueError during data preparation Check that exposure is positive, frequency weights are whole counts, and the subset has one Boolean per input row.
KeyError during data preparation Check the names of the requested fixed-effect and weight columns against the data.
IdentificationError Variation after accounting for all fixed effects and the remaining regressors.
ExistenceError Separation and other obstacles to a finite solution.
ConvergenceError The last numerical state, assessment and solver controls.
SolverCapabilityError Whether the requested solver handles the formula, variance and data options.

Powermean exceptions and warnings provide an identifier for programmatic inspection and fields and message for details. ExistenceError and ConvergenceError also carry status, certificate and last_state when available. For example, a log fit refuses zero outcomes unless you explicitly request a positive-outcome sample.

import pandas as pd
import powermean as pm

try:
    pm.logols("y ~ x", pd.DataFrame({"y": [0, 2, 4], "x": [1, 2, 3]}))
except pm.SampleError as error:
    print(error.identifier)
    print(error.fields)
sample.zero_outcome_at_order
{'count': 1, 'omega': 0.0}

A fixed effect call is refused

Check whether one valid label per row identifies each block. In gravity, exporter^year is one block. If you cancel, choose an existing block by name. For WZ, check the actual retained sample and the three gravity blocks against the WZ requirements. For optional module-level controls, check the record against the formula, mean order and working variance. Options

When a trend is omitted, inspect its scale on the retained rows. By default, the fixed-effect collinearity check compares the sum of squared values after removing the fixed effects with the sum of squared original values. A ratio at or below 1e-9 counts as absorbed. If a time index has a large arbitrary origin, express it as elapsed time from a meaningful base date before fitting. Subtracting a constant preserves the slope in a model with fixed effects.

In a joint PPML model with two fixed effects and slopes, a worker–firm pattern can separate zero observations even when every worker and every firm has a positive outcome. Powermean checks the proposed direction on the original rows, records the separated observations in the sample ledger, and checks the remaining sample again.

If a fixed-effect fit with zeros reports separation_unresolved, Powermean could not certify which remaining rows support a finite fit. On small designs, when both iterative checks are inconclusive, it uses a sparse linear program to check whether all remaining rows can stay. Fitting continues only if the result satisfies the checks for every slope and fixed-effect level. The program cannot select observations for removal.

Your outcome contains zeros

Keep recorded zero flows in a model of the arithmetic mean. For the log or a negative order, justify a positive-outcome analysis before selecting it. In a joint PPML fit, a pattern of zeros can leave some effects without finite estimates. Inspect the sample ledger and any separation diagnostic. A perfectly absorbed regressor needs a different source of variation.

A regressor can also separate zero outcomes in an ordinary PPML fit without fixed effects. For example, if a category has only zeros, Powermean checks which rows can be removed and fits the remaining observations, including any other zeros they contain. Use fit.sample.reason(i) for the exclusion reason at input position i and fit.sample.positions for the fitted rows.

For Gamma PML (tau=2), the same pattern can leave the criterion with no finite optimum. A proved direction gives no_finite_root. With on_failure="return", inspect the diagnostic in fit.certificate. The sample stays intact and the result has no reportable coefficients or standard errors.

A joint fit with profiled fixed effects can return a result with a NumericalWarning about a very small fitted mean at a zero outcome. In this case, a fresh separation check proved overlap on the same retained rows, and the final fixed-effect calculation and all strict accuracy checks passed. The warning remains visible because a very small fitted mean can still deserve attention in the fitted model. Inspect the warning and result.provenance. If overlap remains unresolved or a final check fails, the fit follows the usual failure handling and withholds standard errors.

IOLS reports a slope below its scale floor

If IOLS reports that a slope SD fell below its normalization floor, inspect the recorded scales in result.provenance.failure with on_failure="return". Rescaling that predictor or using Newton can preserve the fitted model. IOLS scale diagnostics

Standard errors are withheld

With on_failure="return", inspect the status, summary and numerical assessment. A returned last iterate with a failed assessment has no reportable uncertainty. A successful fit can still have a degenerate or undefined entry for a particular inference request. Look at the relevant row in tidy() and the covariance conditions.

CoverageWarning refers to the theory supporting the selected numerical route. NumericalWarning and CovarianceWarning describe the fitted calculation and inference diagnostics. Preserve those messages along with the result when reporting a problem.

Results differ from another package

First match the outcome, actual fitted rows, slopes, effect blocks and estimator. Then match the clustering, small-sample factors, reference distribution and final numerical accuracy. Compare with ppmlhdfe

If the issue persists, keep both calls and use a small example someone else can run. Report a problem

GMM1 and GMM2 fits

  • For SampleError, check the counts of every row/column pair and make sure model values are finite. For directed links, use matching agent labels in both identifiers, exclude self-links, and supply every ordered pair of different agents.
  • For IdentificationError, check that slopes vary in rectangle contrasts and that eligible rectangles contain positive products. A Jacobian refusal means the equation has insufficient resolved slope information at the evaluated point.
  • ConvergenceError identifies the numerical failure in status. For an iteration limit or line-search refusal, inspect the supplied start and the last evaluated slope state when available. An unusable_covariance refusal means that the projection did not yield a finite, resolved full covariance. GMM1 and GMM2 estimation and covariance

Report a reproducible problem

After troubleshooting, a small reproducible example lets another reader examine the same behavior. Use the project’s issue tracker if you have access. Reports should exclude confidential data and credentials.

Include enough to reproduce the behavior

State what you expected and what happened, using the model definition or a matched software comparison where relevant. Include the Powermean version, Python and dependency versions, operating system, exact formula and options, and the complete exception identifier and message. For a local build, include the source commit or the distribution filename and its SHA-256 digest. If the fit returned a result with a failure status, include that status.

Use a small simulated or redistributable dataset with the same essential structure. Keep meaningful zeros, FE block relationships and dependence units; do not replace the problem by a different successful model. Save the random seed if data are simulated.

For a fixed-effect fit, include the organization and explicit control records, cancelled and retained block names, sample changes and requested covariance. For a comparison, provide both packages’ calls and conventions. For a runtime report, state the timing boundary, thread setting and repetitions.

Record versions without sharing credentials

Run this in the environment where you used Powermean:

import platform
from importlib.metadata import version

print("Python", platform.python_version())
for package in ("powermean", "numpy", "scipy", "pandas", "formulaic", "within-py"):
    print(package, version(package))

From a Git checkout, git rev-parse HEAD gives its commit. For an installed source distribution or wheel, give the file name and its SHA-256 digest. Identify the build you used. A version number alone cannot distinguish local builds from different revisions.

Remove access tokens, credentials, personal identifiers, local private paths and confidential rows before posting. Do not attach an entire environment, private research archive or account log. A minimal reproducible example is more useful than a large unrelated dump.

The report should preserve the original statistical question and settings. Changing a sample, assumption or tolerance just to obtain success can conceal the problem. When citing an expected method result, use the method source map to identify the relevant version and assumptions.

Read validation and performance evidence

After interpreting a result, ask what supports the claim you want to make. A small equation residual supports numerical accuracy at a computed point. A simulation study addresses sampling behavior in its specified design. A benchmark measures a task on a particular system. Each answers a different question.

Use this page to read model diagnostics, compare results and time a complete analysis.

Begin with the claim

Question Relevant evidence Limit of that evidence
Does a calculation match the intended formula? Independent derivation and direct calculation, including full covariance and SE. Agreement on tested cases does not establish public integration or repeated-sample behavior.
Does the software detect selected invalid inputs or wrong calculations? Perturbations and invalid-input checks. Passing those checks does not rule out every possible defect.
Do two packages agree? Reference comparison with matched data, model, covariance and numerical accuracy. Agreement does not transfer to unmatched conventions or other designs.
How does an estimator behave across samples? A specified Monte Carlo study. Its bias and coverage findings are specific to the design.
How long does the analysis take? A complete fit benchmark with stated hardware, threads and timing boundaries. Runtime does not establish correct inference or a universal speed ranking.
Does installation work in an environment? Installation and platform checks. A tested environment does not validate every future dependency combination.

What the guide currently demonstrates

The gravity example illustrates a coefficient, pair-clustered standard error and interval on one simulated PPML sample. Use its script to reproduce the calculation. The IOLS example shows how to check whether the installed package used the compiled or NumPy implementation.

Read statistical summaries with their failures

To interpret a repeated experiment, identify its target, data-generating process, sample sizes, independent units, repetitions and each method’s assumptions. Read bias, dispersion, reported standard errors and interval coverage together.

A summary restricted to successful fits must state that denominator and also report the overall failure rate and reasons. Replacing failed estimates by zero or silently dropping them changes the evidence. A larger sample alone also does not validate a covariance formula: short panels and growing numbers of effects require the relevant information and dependence conditions.

Compare runtime on matched tasks

For PPML, use omega=1, tau=1 in Powermean and match the other package’s rows, regressors, effects and uncertainty calculation. State elapsed time, threads, repetitions and the timing boundary. A complete fit includes preparation, solving, final numerical assessment, covariance and storing the result. Compare cold fits with cold fits and prepared fits with prepared fits. Report unsuccessful fits and their timings separately.

Use the full analysis elapsed time to compare user workflows. Coming from ppmlhdfe explains how to align the inputs and settings.

The model reference describes the available requests. To share a reproducible example, see Report a problem.

Papers and methods

Benatia, David, Christophe Bellégo and Louis-Daniel Pape (2026). Dealing with Logs and Zeros in Regression Models, arXiv:2203.11820v4, 16 November 2026. The supplemental references below use the ancillary PDF from that same revision. Paper · Supplemental appendices · Replication materials

Topic Sections in Benatia et al. (2026)
Proportional effects §2 and Supplemental Appendix S1.1, including covariance identity (S1.2) and positive-outcome decomposition (S1.4).
Mean order and working variance §§3.1–3.3, equation (3.4) and Propositions 2–3.
IOLS computation §4 and Supplemental Appendix S2. See §3.2 for the estimating equation.
Cancellation §5.1, Proposition 7, Supplemental Appendix S3.3 and S3.6.1. Equations (S3.18) and (S3.19) compare cancellation and joint profiling.
Bias from retained effects §5.2, Theorem 2 and Appendix C.2. Equation (5.7) is the empirical group correction.
Delete-group and higher-order covariance Supplemental Appendix S3.4.2, Proposition S12, and S3.4.3, Proposition S13.

Two-way exponential regression

Jochmans, Koen (2017). Two-Way Models for Gravity. The Review of Economics and Statistics 99, 478–485. See §II for the difference moments and cell-projection inference (Theorem 2), and §III for GMM1 and GMM2. Published paper · Open manuscript · Powermean implementation

The separate three-way PPML correction

Weidner, Martin and Thomas Zylkin (2021). Bias and consistency in three-way gravity models. Journal of International Economics 132, 103513. Section 3 sets out the fixed-TT model and the asymptotic result. Sections 3.4.2 and 3.4.3 give the analytical coefficient correction and pair covariance adjustment. Powermean’s WZ calls use those analytical procedures. Published article · Open-access copy

Panel difference-in-differences

  • Wooldridge, Jeffrey M. (1999). Distribution-free estimation of some nonlinear panel data models. Journal of Econometrics 90(1), 77–97. See the mean-based argument for conditional Poisson fixed effects. Article
  • Wooldridge, Jeffrey M. (2023). Simple approaches to nonlinear difference-in-differences with panel data. The Econometrics Journal 26(3), C31–C66. Section 2 introduces the two-period case. Section 3 gives the staggered conditional index assumptions, pooled estimation and comparison with exponential unit FE. Article
  • Wooldridge, Jeffrey M. (2025). Two-way fixed effects, the two-way Mundlak regression, and difference-in-differences estimators. Empirical Economics. The linear extended TWFE specification allows effects to differ across cohorts and post-treatment dates. Article
  • Rios-Avila, Fernando. Stata jwdid documentation and implementation. Nonlinear models and postestimation · Command source

Record the exact Powermean build with your analysis. For using third-party software, see the Powermean license, scikit-learn notice and native extension notices.

Build or read the guide

The HTML guide is the complete reading document. Open it in a current browser. Its style, navigation scripts and MathML equations are included; reading it does not require a connection. Keep it in the unpacked source distribution to follow links to accompanying files. Links to papers may need a connection.

The matching Quarto document contains the full guide text. The individual Markdown chapters remain the editing source. After changing a chapter, assemble and render the document from the repository root:

node docs/build-guide.mjs
quarto render docs/guide.qmd --to html
node docs/build-guide.mjs --check

Quarto is a documentation authoring tool, not a Powermean runtime dependency. The earlier checked render used Quarto 1.10.18. Rendering does not execute the Python examples. The Markdown chapters hold the captured console output and package-generated tables. Images are embedded in the reading copy. To refresh an example, run its displayed Python in an installed Powermean environment before rendering, and save figure outputs under docs/assets/.

The build script checks that the Markdown outline and offline guide list the same chapters in the same five groups. It refreshes chapter navigation and resolves links inside the combined document. guide.css supplies local presentation styles. Commit the chapter changes, regenerated guide.qmd and rendered guide.html together so the source and reading copy remain synchronized.
